A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FPO research. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gemma-2 experiments, including benchmark comparisons, accuracy/diversity measurements, memory consumption, and ablations in Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds capability-control results in Section 5.3 and additional baseline and multilayer comparisons in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The core FPO objective, cached reference information, and SAE-based MSE constraint remain unchanged. Section 5.3 adds a targeted-control procedure that selects domain-relevant features and applies feature-specific beta settings of 0 or 1, extending how the constraints are applied.

E1.justification: The original training and benchmark coverage remains. Section 5.3 adds instruction-format, multilingual, safety, and financial-sentiment control evaluations using IFEval, MultiAlpaca, WildChat, MKQA, Jailbreak Bench, AdvBench, and Twitter Financial News Sentiment.

E2.justification: Appendix D.1 and Table 6 introduce an evaluated SimPO+KL comparator alongside FPO, SimPO, and TDPO-2. The original benchmark comparator set—SFT, DPO, TDPO-1, TDPO-2, and SimPO—is retained.

E3.justification: The added control experiments introduce feature-specific interventions and formatting accuracy, language-output rates, attack success rates, and sentiment ratios. Their settings include learning rate 2e-5, batch size 64, maximum sequence length 2048, and cosine scheduling with 10% warmup. The original Section 4 and Table 5 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original layer-placement, SAE-type, alpha, stop-gradient, and temperature analyses are retained. v2 adds selective feature-intervention studies across four capability domains and a multilayer SAE ablation testing whether constraining several layers improves alignment, including combinations absent from v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing averaging of GPU memory over 1,000 training steps is retained, and the new tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, memory, and single-layer ablation values are retained. New results include French output rates of 80% versus 3% under different feature constraints (Table 4), FPO/SimPO+KL WR of 51.8/50.8 and WR-L of 50.2/50.6 (Table 6), and accuracy of 64.1 for layer 25 versus 51.4 for layers 0, 12, and 25 (Table 7).

T1.justification: Appendix B's theorem, assumptions, and proof are substantively unchanged. Section 3 changes the stated TDPO storage complexity from O(2NTV) to O(2NV). The normalized-margin derivation also changes non-equivalently: v2 Equation 9 subtracts a reference-margin term after already including reference probabilities in the log ratios.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central novelty, efficiency, stability, controllability, and benchmark-improvement claims. The conclusion is shortened but preserves the central contribution; the new experiments do not materially revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets feature interventions as precise control over particular capabilities while preserving unrelated abilities, extending the earlier accuracy/diversity interpretation. Appendix D also interprets multilayer degradation as evidence favoring single-layer simplicity and more stable alignment.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-access link and documents feature identification and training settings for the new control experiments. The original detailed training table remains. v1's general Reproducible Statement is removed, without removing its concrete hyperparameter table.

R1.justification: v1's dedicated Related Work section is deleted without an appendix replacement. This removes substantive discussion of superposition, mechanistic interpretability, and earlier feature-based alignment research, together with citations including Elhage et al., Marks et al., and Yan et al.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled Constrain Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders. Its structure removes Related Work and the Reproducible Statement, adds Section 5.3, an Impact Statement and Acknowledgement, and expands the appendices with explanatory examples and additional experiments. Much retained methodological prose remains similar.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column review format to a two-column proceedings layout. The original Table 3 is merged into Table 2, the ablation table is rearranged, and the temperature panel moves from Figure 4 to Figure 3. New Tables 4, 6, and 7 display the added experiments.

improvement.justification: The new control experiments, SimPO+KL comparison, multilayer ablation, and code link add useful evidence and access information. However, v2 removes substantial research context and introduces clarity problems: Equation 9 double-counts the reference-margin subtraction, while Table 6 leaves the win-rate reference unclear and bolds FPO's 50.2 WR-L despite SimPO+KL's 50.6. These tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
